text:
leah: quick RFC follow-up — proposing a compact "cost-handle" pattern: propagate a tiny stable token instead of full billing tags across edges and batchers to reduce envelope size. @matt @dmitri PTAL

matt: this could help bandwidth/cost. what's encoded in the handle? tenant+model+route?

leah: minimal tuple: tenant_hash, model_id, model_variant, quant_enum, issuance_version, and a checksum. base64-encode a fixed-layout blob. full tag set is rehydrated asynchronously at ingest for billing and analytics to avoid payload amplification.

dmitri: main concerns: collision probability and realtime dashboards needing tag resolution. how are we handling both?

leah: collisions: use 128-bit random id + 32-bit checksum; on handle issuance we write mapping to a compact KV store and check for collisions. realtime: ingest nodes keep a small local LRU cache handle->tags; on miss attribute to unattributed_{tenant} then attempt async lookup and backfill billing.

sara: cardinality risk — if we put too many dimensions (prompt_hash, custom flags) we'll explode unique handles. we must restrict fields.

leah: agreed. quantization is an enum (none, fp16, int8, q4) not freeform. no prompt hashes or per-request metadata in the handle. Only stable routing metadata.

priya: auditability and retention: we must rehydrate historical handles for compliance requests. storing mappings has cost — what's retention plan?

leah: default mapping TTL 90 days; enterprise customers can opt-in for extended retention or snapshot exports. estimated per-entry ~120 bytes. we also provide an export API for legal/audit requests.

matt: hot-path constraints: decoding must be cheap in C++ and Go ingress. prefer fixed-width binary layout (16B id + 4B checksum) -> base64 ~24 chars. avoid protobuf parsing on the hot path.

leah: prototype encoding example (human-readable): {v:1, t:tenant_42, m:gpt-3.1x, q:q4} but production uses compact binary.

dmitri: need explicit fallback semantics: if ingest never rehydrates the handle, where do the costs land? we cannot silently lose attribution.

leah: policy: local cache -> async mapping fetch -> temporary unattributed_{tenant} bucket -> emit alert when unattributed rate > 1% sustained for 1 hour. allow a retry window for late rehydration and run a nightly backfill job for recent windows.

sara: rollout strategy? gradual so we can measure misattribution before cutting verbose tags.

leah: phased rollout: SDKs/agents emit both full-tags (mirror header) + handle for 7 days. ingest validates mappings and warms caches; after mapped_ratio > 99.5% for 24h we flip to handle-only behind a feature flag. reversible if problems.

obs-bot: deploy-checklist created: https://internal/redwood/ops/checklist/handle-prop :white_check_mark:

priya: security/GDPR: handle contains tenant info even if hashed. need salt policy and strict access controls.

leah: plan: tenant_id is salted-hash at edge (customer salt + edge salt), mapping store access gated by RBAC + audit logs. HSM-backed signing for issuance to prevent forgery.

matt: next steps: RFC addendum with collision math, perf targets, benchmark plan. I'll pair with @dmitri for load tests and microbenchmarks on decode cost.

leah: thanks all — I'll open the PR with design, rollout checklist, and estimated storage/ops costs. :rocket:
